why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 2 to 6 stay within their words. For example, Check 3's "stdout still contains the bad-row lines" follows from "other files still checked and reported", and the usage-message and read-before-check tests are correctly listed under Advisory. Check 1 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires that "A file named twice is reported twice", and its test run names `$T/bad.jsonl` twice. The expect line says nothing about duplicate arguments. "Checks every file named in order" does not force a duplicate to be reported twice, so this is an edge-case test the words don't require. It belongs under Advisory. Check 1 also fixes the single-file output to `$T/bad.jsonl:2: <JSON.parse message>`. That ties the result to one error source, which is stricter than "as for one file before".
